To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the core-shell bimetals have higher stability than their monometals and the C atoms prefer staying on the shell of bimetal particles.
the icosahedral 13-and 55-atom bimetallic Fe-Ni core shell particles have higher stability, and the C atoms prefer staying on the bimetal surfaces.
the icosahedral 13 and 55- atom Fe and Fe-NI core-shell nanoparticles have higher stability than their corresponding monometal nanoparticles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the stability, electronic structure, catalytic properties and interaction of carbon atom with 13- and/or 55-atom mono- and bi-metallic Fe and Fe-NI core-shell nanoparticles.
the stability of icosahedral Fe and Fe-NI core-shell particles and the interaction with carbon atoms.
the stability of the Fe and Ni monometallic nanoparticles as well as the Fe-Ni bimetallic core-shell nanoparticles and the interaction between these nanoparticles and the carbon atoms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the icosahedral Fe-Ni core/shell bimetallic particle has higher stability, weaker interaction with C atom, and more uniform charge distribution than the monometal particles.
the bimetal catalysts have higher stability and lower interaction with C atoms than the monometal catalysts.

the Fe-Ni core shell nanoparticles are more stable than the monometal Fe and Ni particles and have lower interaction with C atoms, which may be the reason why Fe-Ni core-shells are better SWCNT catalysts than Fe and Ni.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the icosahedral 13-, 55- and 147-atom Fe, Ni, and Fe-Ni particles are stable, and the icosahedrally symmetric Fe-Ni core-shells particles have higher stability.
the bimetal catalysts are more stable than the monometal catalysts.

the 13- and the 55-atom icosahedral Fe-Ni core shell bimetallic nanoparticles are more stable than the corresponding monomeric Fe and Ni particles; the Fe surface shell displays a positive charge while the Ni surface shell exhibits a negative charge; C atoms prefer staying on the bimetalic surface, while C atoms prefer locating at the subsurface of monometallic particle.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the bimetal Fe-Ni core shell particles are more stable than the corresponding monatomic particles, and that the bimetic particles are more likely to catalyze the growth of SWCNTs than the monatomic particles.

the icosahedral Fe-Ni core/shell particles are more stable than the corresponding mononuclear particles and the interaction of the core/shell particles with carbon atoms is much weaker than that of the mononuclear particles.
the core-shell bimetals have stronger stability and higher chemical activity, which is beneficial for SWCNT growth.
